A realistic logbook: reef, sediment and pelagic tactics

Henning Winker

This example applies the whole toolbox to a simulated logbook that looks like real data: ten species, discrete fishing tactics, trips that combine sets, rounding, under-reporting, a species recorded under two names, missing positions, fleet turnover and a closure. Because the data are simulated, the true tactics and the true biomass trends are known, so we can check what each step recovers.

The simulated fishery

simulate_logbook() combines the spatial multispecies simulator with the habitat-based tactics of Winker et al. (2014).

  • Habitats. Depth increases offshore (shelf to slope) and the substrate is patchy: reef patches within sediment. Demersal densities are depth preference x substrate affinity, which gives four habitats as continuous gradients: shallow reef, deep reef, shallow sediment and deep sediment. Pelagic species follow sea temperature and distance offshore and migrate seasonally through the area.
  • Tactics. Each trip chooses a tactic (Reef bottom handline, Sediment bottom longline, or Pelagic troll) and a place to fish, by expected value. Demersal specialist vessels cannot fish pelagic, pelagic specialists only fish pelagic, the other vessels choose freely.
  • Changes over time. Demersal prices are high in 2000-2007, pelagic prices boom in 2008-2015, then prices are neutral; from 2016 the sediment gear is banned deeper than 300 m and effort is cut. Some vessels enter later (and are more efficient), others leave.
sim <- simulate_logbook(seed = 1)
knitr::kable(sim$settings$species[, c("species", "group", "habitat", "depth_mu",
                                      "price")], row.names = FALSE)
species group habitat depth_mu price
Dentex dentex demersal shallow reef 60 12
Pagellus erythrinus demersal shallow sediment 50 8
Pagellus bogaraveo demersal deep reef 350 15
Merluccius merluccius demersal deep sediment 400 5
Conger conger demersal reef, all depths 150 3
Phycis blennoides demersal deep, mixed 500 2
Thunnus alalunga pelagic offshore 700 6
Coryphaena hippurus pelagic warm, offshore 300 7
Seriola dumerili pelagic coastal, reef-associated 100 9

Steps 1-4: format and explore

x <- cpue_data(sim$logbook, year = "year", species = "species", catch = "kg",
               effort = "hours", id = "trip", vessel = "vessel",
               lon = "lon", lat = "lat", covariates = "month",
               synonyms = c("Blackspot seabream" = "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
x <- subset(x, !is.na(lon), note = "positions reported")
x
## <cpue_data> 20996 operations, 10 species, years 2000 - 2024 
##   vessels: 40 
##   effort: hours 
##   position: lon / lat 
##   covariates: month 
##   main species: Scomber colias, Dentex dentex, Pagellus bogaraveo, Pagellus erythrinus, Conger conger ... 
## Processing log:
##                 step operations                             note
##  input (long format)      21399       114027 records, 10 species
##               subset      20996 positions reported (403 removed)
fl <- plot_fleet(x)
fl$vessels

fl$vessel_years

plot_species_curve(x, threshold = 0.95)

x <- select_species(x, threshold = 0.95)
plot_composition(x)

Here we can check the clusters against the true tactic of each trip (the tactic of its first set):

true_tactic <- sim$trips$tactic[match(x$data$trip, sim$trips$trip)]
table(cluster = x$data$FT, true = true_tactic)
##        true
## cluster Pelagic Reef Sediment
##       1    3315 1563     1119
##       2     492 3170     1890
##       3     503 3205     1749
##       4    3223  376      391
pt <- plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)
pt$time

pt$pcs_time

pt$map_tactic

Steps 7-9: standardise two species

Blackspot seabream (deep reef)

Blackspot seabream lives on deep reefs and is caught mainly by the reef tactic, whose use changes with prices.

fit_sbr <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo",
                    models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_sbr)
##       model component     n      AIC      BIC dev_explained   edf tweedie_p
## 1      Base      main 20996 131776.9 132301.1        0.1396  63.9     1.840
## 2    Base+S      main 20996 128375.4 129194.7        0.3095 100.9     1.816
## 3 Cluster+S      main 20996 124179.0 125020.6        0.4902 103.6     1.783
## 4     DPC+S      main 20996 118362.9 119237.1        0.6500 107.6     1.775
##   vessel_sd    dAIC
## 1     2.489 13414.0
## 2     2.227 10012.4
## 3     1.115  5816.0
## 4     0.437     0.0
plot_index(fit_sbr, true = logbook_truth(sim, "Pagellus bogaraveo"))

plot_influence(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")

Dolphinfish (seasonal pelagic migrant)

Dolphinfish is caught by the pelagic tactic and is only present in summer, so month is added as a cyclic smoother.

fit_dol <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Coryphaena hippurus",
                    models = c("Base", "Covariates", "Cluster", "DPC"),
                    terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                    knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                    vessel = TRUE, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_dol)
##        model component     n      AIC      BIC dev_explained  edf tweedie_p
## 1       Base      main 20996 162090.6 162614.3        0.1957 63.8     1.869
## 2 Covariates      main 20996 159509.3 160064.7        0.2757 67.8     1.859
## 3    Cluster      main 20996 157763.2 158341.6        0.3298 70.7     1.850
## 4        DPC      main 20996 136129.8 136743.1        0.7759 74.9     1.739
##   vessel_sd    dAIC
## 1     1.738 25960.8
## 2     1.652 23379.5
## 3     1.204 21633.3
## 4     0.277     0.0
plot_index(fit_dol, true = logbook_truth(sim, "Coryphaena hippurus"))

plot_effects(fit_dol, "DPC")$numeric

plot_vessel_effects(fit_dol, "DPC")

Things to try

  • logbook_settings() lists every setting; change prices, the closure, the share of two-set trips (logbook$two_sets), the reef share, or make all vessels flexible to see how each affects the targeting covariates.
  • Compare n_pc and the number of clusters, and the species set (select_species(..., pool_other = TRUE)).
  • Fit a delta model (family = "delta_lognormal") for species with many zeros.

References

Winker, H., Kerwath, S.E. and Attwood, C.G. (2014) Proof of concept for a novel procedure to standardize multispecies catch and effort data. Fisheries Research 155: 149-159.
